action.sense: Something a control or command does (the action a picker chooses, a dialog's actions, a command's name in the shortcut list).

ai-agent.sense: Cmdr's own AI acting on the user's behalf, including the provenance label on operations it ran.

ai-client.sense: An outside AI app driving Cmdr over its automation interface, named as the source of an operation.

android-platform-tools.sense: Google's Android SDK Platform Tools package, which ships adb.

android-tools.sense: The Android command-line developer tools installed on the Mac, as a group.

blocked.sense: Something held back from proceeding: a proposed rename preflight won't let through, or an access macOS or another process prevents.

busy.sense: Something that can't take a request right now: a volume with operations running, a device, a provider, a system resource.

chip.sense: A small labeled pill in the UI, such as the repository chip that shows a folder is inside a git repo.

coming-soon.sense: A marker on a feature that isn't available yet.

conversation.sense: One thread of messages between the user and Ask Cmdr, as distinct from chatting as an activity.

database.sense: A structured data store (the index database, a provider's database).

debounce.sense: Waiting for a burst of events to settle before acting on them (an advanced setting).

deployment.sense: A named model instance on Azure OpenAI that a request is routed to.

desktop-folder.sense: The macOS Desktop folder, named in lists of protected folders.

exclude.sense: The user deliberately taking a folder out of indexing or a search scope.

file-handle.sense: An open reference an app or process holds on a file, which can keep it alive or locked.

file-manager.sense: The kind of app Cmdr is.

forget.sense: Dropping a saved server, a saved password, a trusted key, or a remembered note so Cmdr no longer keeps it.

git-branch.sense: A git branch, shown in the repo chip and browsable in the .git portal.

git-browser.sense: Cmdr's view that lists a repo's branches, tags, commits, and worktrees like folders.

git-commit.sense: A git commit, as a browsable snapshot.

git-dirty.sense: A git working tree with uncommitted changes.

git-worktree.sense: A git linked checkout (git worktree), including the ones the .git portal lists.

hardlink.sense: Files that share their data through hard links, so a copy writes more than the source takes on disk.

help-menu.sense: The menu bar's Help menu, named in prose (send a report from the Help menu).

history.sense: A record of past items: the file operations Cmdr ran, recent selections, reopenable tabs.

home-folder.sense: The user's home folder, and the Go menu's Home item.

importance.sense: How much a folder matters to the user, which decides what gets indexed first.

interrupted.sense: Something cut off before it could finish by an outside cause (a signal, a dropped connection).

just-now.sense: The newest step of a relative-time label (just now, 5m ago).

key-combination.sense: A set of keys pressed together, as recorded for a shortcut.

last-used.sense: The column that shows when a saved server was last opened.

linux-distribution.sense: A Linux distribution, whose package manager provides a missing package.

mcp-server.sense: Cmdr's Model Context Protocol server that AI assistants can connect to.

model-library.sense: A provider's catalog of downloadable models (the Ollama library).

not-found.sense: Something Cmdr looked for isn't there (a path, a share, a device, the adb binary).

organization.sense: The company a commercial license is issued to.

original.sense: The source copy of a file that a move leaves in place until it knows the destination copy is safe.

owner.sense: The person who runs a server or owns a shared folder, or the account that owns a file.

pattern.sense: A filename, regex, or rename pattern the user or the AI writes.

placeholder.sense: A slot in a title or format string that Cmdr fills in (a date or name token).

problem.sense: A non-fatal issue named in explanatory prose, in Cmdr's calm voice.
problem.note: Cmdr's voice avoids a bare error word; this is the neutral noun for what went wrong.

recent.sense: The latest items the user used (recent searches, recent selections, the latest download, recently closed tabs).

regex.sense: A regular-expression search or selection mode.

register-shortcut.sense: A global hotkey the system accepted (or refused) for Cmdr.

removable.sense: A drive that can be ejected and unplugged, as opposed to an internal one.

rename-cycle.sense: A set of renames that swap names in a loop, so one needs a temporary name.

repository.sense: A git repository (the folder Cmdr shows the repo chip for, or Cmdr's GitHub repo).

reset.sense: Putting a setting back to its default, or zoom back to 100%.

save-panel.sense: The macOS Save dialog Cmdr opens to save content as a file.

sharing-and-permissions.sense: The section of Finder's Get Info window that lists who can read and write an item.

snapshot.sense: A frozen point-in-time copy: a git commit seen as a folder, or an APFS snapshot folder search skips.

stall.sense: A transfer or file fetch that is still alive but has made no progress for a while.

status.sense: The current state of something (a server row, a license, a git file, an index), as a label or column.

subscription.sense: A time-limited commercial license the user renews.

technical-details.sense: The disclosure under an error message that holds the raw system code and message.

wizard.sense: A step-by-step setup flow (the onboarding wizard).

working-tree.sense: The checked-out files of a git repo, in the generic git sense.
